title: The Impact of Observed Deforestation on the Mesoscale Distribution of Rainfall and Clouds in Amazonia

settings.description: MM5V2 nested simulations over Rondonia with a 480 km outer domain at 12 km and a 240 km inner domain at 4 km, 24 sigma levels to 100 hPa, non-hydrostatic, explicit convection on the inner domain, 72 hours from 2000 LT.
Break period 3-6 November 1990, original synoptic wind, uniform forest control run.
Break period, original synoptic wind, observed fish-bone deforestation pattern.
Break period with synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten, uniform forest control run.
Break period with synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten, observed deforestation.
Break period reduced-wind deforestation run repeated at 2 km grid spacing to test resolution sensitivity.
Rainy season 3-6 January 1990, original synoptic wind, uniform forest control run.
Rainy season, original synoptic wind, observed deforestation.
Rainy season with synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten, uniform forest control run.
Rainy season with synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten, observed deforestation.
Dry season 30 June to 3 July 1990, uniform forest control run.
First dry-season simulation day, when synoptic wind was weakest and mesoscale circulations strongest.
Second dry-season simulation day, when synoptic wind was strongest and mesoscale circulations weakest.
Third dry-season simulation day, with a weaker enhancement of afternoon shallow clouds.
The uniformly forested upper-right and lower-left corners of the inner domain, with CAPE of about 600 J and 200 J respectively, used to separate PBL-triggered from mesoscale-triggered clouds.

claims.from: observed deforestation during the break period under original synoptic wind
claims.statement: The model predicted no more than 0.1 mm of three-day cumulative rainfall at isolated locations in the control run and almost none in the deforestation run.

claims.from: observed deforestation during the break period under original synoptic wind
claims.statement: Afternoon cloudiness was not observed in either the control or the deforestation run.

claims.from: observed deforestation
claims.statement: Deforestation induced a well-defined mesoscale heat flux structure whose space-time distribution agreed with earlier studies.

claims.from: observed deforestation pattern
claims.statement: The heterogeneous deforestation pattern induced mesoscale circulations of increased intensity over the deforested domain.

claims.from: mesoscale circulations weak near the 840 hPa most-unstable level
claims.statement: Under original synoptic wind the mesoscale circulations were not strong enough to overcome the sounding energy barrier, being weak and with vanishing mesoscale heat flux near the most-unstable level of about 840 hPa.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. This vertical mismatch is the mechanism explaining the break-period null result.

claims.from: observed deforestation under reduced synoptic wind in the break period
claims.statement: Rainfall patterns in the deforestation and control runs were qualitatively similar, with sporadic rain cells at somewhat different locations that did not resemble the land cover pattern.
claims.match_note: Extracted as no significant difference from control.

claims.from: observed deforestation under reduced synoptic wind
claims.statement: Enhanced cloud was simulated over the deforested locations at levels between 900 and 800 hPa.

claims.from: successive simulation days under reduced synoptic wind
claims.statement: Enhanced cloudiness over the deforested areas also occurred in the afternoons of the second and third simulation days.
claims.match_note: Not extracted, so the persistence of the effect across days is unavailable.

claims.from: synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten
claims.statement: The mesoscale circulations measured by mesoscale heat flux were stronger under the weakened synoptic wind condition.

claims.from: synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten
claims.to: vertical extent of the mesoscale circulation
claims.statement: The circulations reached higher altitudes than the most-unstable level of about 840 hPa under reduced synoptic wind.

claims.from: synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten in the break period
claims.statement: The atmosphere was less stable under reduced synoptic wind, with greater CAPE and smaller convective inhibition.

claims.from: synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten
claims.statement: The weakened synoptic wind environment was the one in which mesoscale circulations were responsible for triggering enhanced afternoon cloudiness over the deforested areas.

claims.from: low-level cumulus clouds over deforested areas under reduced wind
claims.statement: The low-level cumulus clouds produced little precipitation, with sparse rainfall cells that do not overlap the cloud locations, so deforestation may enhance afternoon cloudiness while contributing little local rainfall.

claims.from: 2 km versus 4 km horizontal grid resolution
claims.statement: Cloudiness simulated at 2 km agreed at least qualitatively with the corresponding 4 km simulation.

claims.from: 2 km versus 4 km horizontal grid resolution
claims.statement: Rainfall simulated at 2 km agreed at least qualitatively with the corresponding 4 km simulation.

claims.from: 2 km horizontal grid resolution
claims.statement: The 2 km simulation produced larger rain rates than the 4 km simulation.

claims.from: 2 km horizontal grid resolution
claims.statement: The 2 km simulation produced higher cloud water content than the 4 km simulation.

claims.from: rainy season sounding profile
claims.statement: The rainy-season atmosphere is conditionally unstable with relatively large CAPE, small convective inhibition, and a most-unstable level of about 970 hPa very close to the surface, far more unstable than the break period.
claims.match_note: Not extracted, so the reason the rainy season behaves differently is missing.

claims.from: rainy season conditions
claims.to: deep convection and rainfall in both runs
claims.statement: Active deep convection and intensive rainfall were obtained in both the deforestation and the control runs.

claims.from: observed deforestation versus uniform forest in the rainy season
claims.statement: The distributions of rainfall from the control and deforestation runs were nearly identical in the rainy season.

claims.from: observed deforestation versus uniform forest in the rainy season
claims.statement: The distributions of high clouds from the control and deforestation runs were nearly identical in the rainy season.

claims.from: rainy season conditions
claims.statement: Shallow clouds did not occur at all in the rainy-season simulations.

claims.from: land cover variability in the rainy season
claims.statement: Variability in land cover played no role in shaping the distribution of cloudiness during the rainy season.

claims.from: land cover variability in the rainy season
claims.statement: Variability in land cover played no role in shaping the distribution of rainfall during the rainy season.

claims.from: synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten in the rainy season
claims.statement: The spatial coverage of afternoon cloudiness was greatly reduced under weakened synoptic wind in the rainy season.

claims.from: synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten in the rainy season
claims.statement: The clouds also occurred at different locations under the weakened synoptic wind.

claims.from: reduced synoptic wind in the rainy season
claims.statement: Deep convection still led to high-level clouds above 500 hPa peaking near 300 hPa and no low-level clouds were generated.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. This distinguishes the rainy-season reduced-wind case from the break-period reduced-wind case, which produced low cloud.

claims.from: synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten in the rainy season
claims.statement: The area receiving rainfall shrank considerably, leaving only isolated rainfall cells.

claims.from: synoptic wind reduced by a factor of ten in the rainy season
claims.statement: The reduction is attributed to weakened large-scale ascent and reduced moisture convergence, consistent with a much smaller CAPE and a less unstable atmosphere.

claims.from: land surface processes under reduced synoptic wind in the rainy season
claims.statement: No correlation was found between rainfall and land cover in either run, so land surface processes were irrelevant to the convection processes over this period.

claims.from: mesoscale heat flux essentially zero
claims.statement: Mesoscale circulations did not develop under reduced synoptic wind in the rainy season, because the mesoscale heat flux was essentially zero.

claims.from: departures from the idealised synoptic conditions assumed in the mesoscale heat flux definition
claims.to: the apparent rainy-season original-wind heat flux signal
claims.statement: The apparent mesoscale heat flux under original rainy-season wind is judged an artifact rather than a real signal, because it shows periodicity with height, negative near-surface values, and the wrong dependence on synoptic wind.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. A diagnostic-validity caveat that a naive reader of the graph would miss.

claims.from: dry season conditions
claims.to: three-day cumulative rainfall in both runs
claims.statement: Moderate three-day cumulative rainfall was simulated in both the control and deforestation runs, with an evident difference between the two rainfall patterns.

claims.from: observed deforestation in the dry season
claims.to: rainfall coverage during the first afternoon
claims.statement: Precipitation from the deforestation run had broader coverage than the control during the first afternoon, when localized deep convection occurred over the deforested region.

claims.from: land cover heterogeneity in the dry season
claims.statement: The rainfall organisation reflects a land cover signature, with rain cells slightly shifted north-west of the deforested areas because of the prevailing wind.

claims.from: the second and third dry-season simulation days
claims.to: rainfall pattern relative to land cover
claims.statement: On the second and third days the deforestation-run rainfall patterns looked random, did not reflect land cover, and were not qualitatively different from the control.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. The land cover signature is present on one day out of three, which the extracted claims do not convey.

claims.from: mesoscale circulation over deforested areas in the dry season
claims.statement: An enhancement of shallow cumulus clouds near the 800 hPa level was simulated over the deforested areas in the first afternoon.

claims.from: mesoscale circulation over deforested areas in the dry season
claims.to: precipitating high cumulus clouds near 300 hPa
claims.statement: Enhanced high cumulus clouds near 300 hPa were simulated over the partially cleared areas and, contrary to the non-precipitating shallow clouds, contributed local rainfall.

claims.from: the third dry-season day
claims.statement: A weaker enhancement of afternoon shallow clouds was simulated in the deforestation run on the third day.

claims.from: the enhanced shallow clouds over deforested patches
claims.statement: The enhanced shallow clouds were short lived, lasting about four hours from 1400 LT on the first day and 1500 LT on the third day.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. Duration is exactly the kind of detail a scenario designer needs.

claims.from: the second dry-season afternoon
claims.to: resemblance of low clouds to land cover
claims.statement: Sporadic low clouds occurred in the second afternoon with no resemblance to the land cover pattern.

claims.from: relatively large CAPE of about 600 J over uniformly forested domain corner
claims.to: low-level cloud triggering by PBL turbulence
claims.statement: Low-level clouds in the uniformly forested upper-right corner of both runs were triggered by PBL turbulence rather than mesoscale circulation, since there was no differential heating there.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. This control separates the mesoscale mechanism from ordinary boundary-layer convection.

claims.from: smaller CAPE of about 200 J despite stronger surface heating
claims.statement: The lower-left forested corner remained cloud free despite stronger surface sensible heat flux, because its CAPE was only about 200 J.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. A counterintuitive result: stronger surface heating did not produce cloud where instability was insufficient.

claims.from: the vertical structure of the dry-season heat flux
claims.to: attribution to mesoscale circulation and condensation heating
claims.statement: Below about 750 hPa the flux structure indicates mesoscale circulations, while above it the structure follows the cloud distribution and is attributed to condensation heating during moist convection.

claims.from: negative mesoscale heat flux on the second dry-season afternoon
claims.to: relative strength of moist convection in control versus deforestation
claims.statement: The negative heat flux during the second afternoon indicates that overall moist convection was stronger in the control run than in the deforestation run.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. A reversal in which deforestation weakened rather than enhanced convection.

claims.from: relatively strong synoptic forcing
claims.statement: Mesoscale circulation was strongest on the first dry-season day and weakest on the second, matching the synoptic wind being weakest and strongest respectively, because synoptic wind inhibits mesoscale circulation development.

claims.from: organised mesoscale circulations caused by deforestation
claims.statement: The organised mesoscale circulations caused by deforestation trigger convection that enhances afternoon cloudiness and local rainfall in the dry season.

claims.from: land cover heterogeneity in the dry season
claims.statement: The majority of enhanced shallow clouds formed over the deforested patches, following closely the pattern of land cover.

claims.from: deforestation in Rondonia during the rainy season
claims.statement: The model predicted that deforestation had no effect on rainfall and cloudiness distributions during the rainy season, when mesoscale circulations were inhibited by relatively strong synoptic forcing.

claims.from: relative strength of synoptic-scale, mesoscale and local forcings
claims.to: impact of small-scale deforestation on convection and rainfall
claims.statement: The impact of deforestation at the roughly ten kilometre scale on local convection and rainfall depends on the relative strength of synoptic-scale, mesoscale and local forcings.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. This is the paper's single most transferable statement and the one a scenario designer would most want.
